Simone, it is Lucia. Thank you for agreeing to chair tomorrow's call. Here is who is dialing in. From Madrid, Javier and me. From New York, Ryan, and he is looping in Tom Walsh from the tax side. And from Sao Paulo, Paulo Mendes, our local counsel. That is five people in three cities, plus you, so it will not be easy. Last time, Ryan and Javier talked over each other for ten minutes, and nobody remembers what we decided. So, three things. First, open with the agenda: the new date, the indemnity and the documents. Second, if the interest question gets complicated, park it and come back to it at the end. Tom will want to discuss it for an hour. Third, before you close, check that everyone is on the same page, and send the takeaways in writing the same day. If we have consensus on the date and the indemnity, that is a good call.

Hi Simone, it is Tom Walsh, from the tax side in New York. Thank you for chairing this morning. Honestly, it was the most efficient call we have had on this deal. Before you send the summary, I want to check my notes, because I cut out for a minute in the middle. We agreed on the fifteenth of April for the closing, didn't we? And the indemnity covers the full tax debt. The interest is the one point we parked, and you said we would come back to it on Thursday, didn't you? Paulo is going to send the documents by Friday. If that is correct, then I am on the same page. One small request: next time, can you hand over to me a little earlier? I almost chimed in twice, and I did not want to talk over Javier. Thanks again.

First, before the call, you send the agenda and you check who will dial in. Then, you open the call: you welcome everyone and you say the three points. After that, you hand over to each person by name, and you park any topic that is too big. Next, you check agreement with question tags, like we agreed on April, didn't we? Finally, you close with the takeaways, and you send them in writing the same day.
